name: Southern hawker
note: Southern hawkers (docs 11, 12, 23; M2; Matt chose the species on 2026-10-20): large green and blue dragonflies that patrol and hover over ponds and come to look at people. A few at a time, not individuals with names. LIFE. ecology: kind swarm (src/world/creatures/swarms.js keeps them in the hourly tick); dormancy names the window in recipes/world/seasons.json (from the start of summer, once the water is warm, to mid-autumn they fly; the rest of the year they are nymphs in the pond). needs (src/world/ecology/needs.js): five, each 0..1, mood = their weighted geometric mean. water: still fresh water depthM deep in a body of at least body.minM2 square meters (a puddle is not a pond to breed in), full within okM, none beyond maxM. Sun: they want a sunny pond; nothing shades the island yet, so it is not scored. food: the midge field over a square of radiusM, against per times the ideal group (they share the midges lightly with the frogs). shelter: perches and stems to climb out on as nymphs, each plant weighted, the best within radiusM, from 'from' and full at 'full'. quiet: low sensitivity. company: n[0] to n[2], n[1] ideal. scored: any open ground or fresh water (where: near), for the beat over the pond and its banks. arrival (src/world/creatures/swarms.js, as the minnows'): a pond is right once its best square scores rightScore and it has room for startCount, for rightHoldH hours; after scoutAfterH, on a late morning (comeAtH) while they fly, a pair may come (scoutChance a day, surely by maxWaitDays); one per m2PerOne square meters of good water, up to company n[2]; they settle after settleAfterH at settleMood, grow by growShare of the room left each day while content, and are happy after happyHoldH hours with happyMin at happyMood. In their dormancy window nothing changes. gift: springs, the Water tool's Spring mode (unlocks.springs; docs 12, 13).
_look: LOOK (M2 piece F). body: a blended-SDF southern hawker in real meters, body-local +z forward, origin at the middle of the thorax (it flies, so nothing stands on the ground): a small head with two large eyes, an ellipsoid thorax, a long thin abdomen, four flat wings, each on its own bone (wing.fl, wing.fr fore, wing.hl, wing.hr hind) pivoting at the thorax; bones listed here (no rig code). Wings are thicker than life (about 2 mm) so the mesh keeps them at its coarser levels of detail. displayScale 2.5 as the frogs (Matt, 2026-10-21: drawn larger so players can find them); contactShadow 0. albedo (physical, linear): a dark body with blue-green spots (blotch), large blue-green eyes, smoky clear wings; wetSpecular: the glossy shell. motion (src/world/creatures/patrol.js; live only): kind patrol; each keeps a beat of beatPoints hold points within beatM of its group's home, over the water where there is any, hoverHeightM over the water or ground; it hovers hoverS seconds (bobbing bobM at bobHz), then darts to another point at up to dartMps (easing dartEase m/s per meter left, turning with agility); with perchChance after a hover, and at night, it rests on a reed or rush tip within perchReachM (perchOn: how tall each plant's tip stands at full size, perched at perchShare of it) for perchS seconds; never lower than clearM over the water or ground; banks rollPerAccel per m/s² of turning, at most maxRoll; wings beat wingHz (hovering, darting) times a second, swinging wingSwing radians, the hind pair hindLag radians behind the fore, drooping restDroop on a perch. A startle (presence) sends it fleeing up to fleeHeightM for fleeS seconds. presence (doc 23; real meters): ringM, calmSpeed, editReachM as the minnows'. find: tap within tapM (plus tapPerM per meter away), or keep one within lookM of the middle of the view, zoomed in to lookDistM, for holdS seconds.
_known: Dragonflies can't be named, so their gift comes when they first know you to presence.knownTrust (Matt, October 27, 2026; src/world/creatures/swarms.js knownNow). The moment (patrol.js land): if you are on foot, the nearest one flies to you and rests on top of your hat (hatM above your head) for restS real seconds, or until you move motion.landMoveM.

voice.note: The wings' sound (doc 25 'Creature voices', model wing-rattle; src/audio/voices/dragonfly.js, played by src/audio/voices.js setFlyers). One voice per flying dragonfly within reach, nearest ones only (nearest), each at its own place. SOUND: a seeded loop of beats wingbeats at baseHz; each beat is a grain of noise falling 60 dB in grainMs, then the hind pair's grain hindLag radians later at hindShare of it, each grain up to unevenness weaker at random and up to jitter of a beat early or late, with a tiny extra crinkle in crinkle of the beats: a dry papery rattle, not a hum. The loop plays at the motion's wingHz (hovering, darting; from the motion block, not here), each dragonfly up to rateJitter faster or slower. highpassHz takes out the low end; a lowpass opens from lowpassHz[0] hovering to [1] darting; body is a low band (hz, q, db) for the thrum of the beat. LEVEL: hoverDb hovering, dartDb at the motion's dartMps (in between by the square root of the share of it, so a dart soon sounds like one), following over rampS seconds; on a perch it fades to silence over perchRampS. REACH: inverse distance from refDistance with a steep rolloff, and a hard fade from fadeFromM to reachM (about 2 m) so only one passing close by the camera is heard. Distances are from the camera eye.

ecology._pond: A pond of their own (Matt, 2026-10-20): they come only to a pond the player made, with no fish in it (src/world/ecology/coarse.js pondFit). fishFree: no group of this species (minnows) lives in it; if one moves in, the dragonflies' mood falls and they thin and move on as from any unhappy pond. shallowShare of its squares are shallowM deep (mostly shallow). At least marginM2 square meters of margin marginM deep where the player moved the ground shapedCm or more from the island as generated (dug, or a Cliff tool Terrace), with cover grown in there (shelter, from the cover weights above, marginCover or more). No starting pond qualifies: the island as generated has no shaped ground at all, so its ponds have no shaped margin (tools/ecology-lab.html, unit tests).
ecology._grace: A9 (Matt, 2026-10-21): when a settled group's pond starts failing it (a rain-fed pond lowered in summer so its shaped margin is dry, fish moved in, too little cover), it grows uneasy and waits arrival.leaveGraceDays game days before it thins or moves on; the journal says why and Show me rings the pond (src/world/creatures/swarms.js). A gently shelving bank keeps a margin at any level.
